1.1: The Parables of Salomon the sonne of David King of Israel,
1.2: To know wisdom, and instruction, to understand ye wordes of knowledge,
1.3: To receive instruction to do wisely, by justice and iudgement and equitie,
1.4: To give unto the simple, sharpenesse of wit, and to the child knowledge and discretion.
1.5: A wise man shall hear and increase in learning, and a man of understanding shall attayne unto wise counsels,
1.6: To understand a parable, and the interpretation, the wordes of ye wise, and their dark sayings.
1.7: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fooles despise wisedome and instruction.
1.8: My sonne, hear thy fathers instruction, and forsake not thy mothers teaching.
1.9: For they shalbe a comely ornament unto thine head, and as chaines for thy neck.
1.10: My sonne, if sinners doe intise thee, consent thou not.
1.11: If they say, Come with us, we will lay wait for blood, and lie priuilie for the innocent without a cause:
1.12: We wil swallow them up alive like a grave even whole, as those that goe down into the pit:
1.13: We shall find all precious riches, and fill our houses with spoyle:
1.14: Cast in thy lot among us: we will all have one purse:
1.15: My sonne, walk not thou in the way with them: refrain thy foot from their path.
1.16: For their feet runne to evil, and make haste to shed blood.
1.17: Certainely as without cause the net is spred before the eyes of all that hath wing:
1.18: So they lay wait for blood and lie privily for their lives.
1.19: Such are the wayes of every one that is greedy of gain: he would take away the life of the owners thereof.
1.20: Wisdom cryeth without: she uttereth her voyce in the streetes.
1.21: She calleth in the hye street, among the prease in the entrings of the gates, and uttereth her wordes in the citie, saying,
1.22: O ye foolish, how long will ye love foolishnes? and the scornefull take their pleasure in scorning, and the fooles hate knowledge?
1.23: (Turn you at my correction: loe, I will powre out my mind unto you, and make you understand my wordes)
1.24: Because I have called, and ye refused: I have stretched out mine hand, and none would regard.
1.25: But ye have despised all my counsel, and would none of my correction.
1.26: I will also laugh at your destruction, and mock, when your fear cometh.
1.27: Whe your fear cometh like sudden desolation, and your destruction shall come like a whirle wind: whe affliction and anguish shall come upon you,
1.28: Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer: they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me,
1.29: Because they hated knowledge, and did not chuse the fear of the Lord.
1.30: They would none of my counsel, but despised all my correction.
1.31: Therefore shall they eat of ye fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own deuises.
1.32: For ease slaieth the foolish, and the prosperitie of fooles destroyeth them.
1.33: But he that obeyeth me, shall dwell safely, and be quiet from fear of evil.

2.1: My sonne, if thou wilt receive my wordes, and hide my commandements within thee,
2.2: And cause thine eares to hearken unto wisdom, and encline thine heart to understanding,
2.3: (For if thou callest after knowledge, and cryest for understanding:
2.4: If thou seekest her as silver, and searchest for her as for treasures,
2.5: Then shalt thou understand the fear of the Lord, and find the knowledge of God.
2.6: For the Lord giveth wisdom, out of his mouth cometh knowledge and understanding.
2.7: He preserveth the state of the righteous: he is a shield to them that walk uprightly,
2.8: That they may keep the wayes of iudgement: and he preserveth the way of his Saintes)
2.9: Then shalt thou understand righteousnes, and iudgement, and equitie, and every good path.
2.10: When wisdom entreth into thine heart, and knowledge deliteth thy soul,
2.11: Then shall counsel preserve thee, and understanding shall keep thee,
2.12: And deliver thee from the evil way, and from the man that speaketh froward things,
2.13: And from them that leave the wayes of righteousnes to walk in the wayes of darkenes:
2.14: Which reioyce in doing evil, and delite in the frowardness of the wicked,
2.15: Whose wayes are crooked and they are lewd in their paths.
2.16: And it shall deliver thee from the strange woman, even from the stranger, which flattereth with her wordes.
2.17: Which forsaketh the guide of her youth, and forgetteth the covenant of her God.
2.18: Surely her house tendeth to death, and her paths unto the dead.
2.19: All they that goe unto her, return not again, neither take they hold of the wayes of life.
2.20: Therefore walk thou in the way of good men, and keep the wayes of the righteous.
2.21: For the just shall dwell in the land, and the upright men shall remain in it.
2.22: But the wicked shalbe cut off from ye earth, and the transgressours shalbe rooted out of it.

3.1: My sonne, forget not thou my Law, but let thine heart keep my commandements.
3.2: For they shall increase the length of thy dayes and the yeeres of life, and thy prosperitie.
3.3: Let not mercie and trueth forsake thee: bind them on thy neck, and write them upon the table of thine heart.
3.4: So shalt thou find fauour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
3.5: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart, and lean not unto thine own wisdom.
3.6: In all thy wayes acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy wayes.
3.7: Be not wise in thine own eyes: but fear the Lord, and depart from evil.
3.8: So health shalbe unto thy navel, and marowe unto thy bones.
3.9: Honour the Lord with thy riches, and with the first fruites of all thine increase.
3.10: So shall thy barnes be filled with abundance, and thy presses shall burst with new wine.
3.11: My sonne, refuse not the chastening of the Lord, neither be grieved with his correction.
3.12: For the Lord correcteth him, whom he loveth, even as the father doeth the child in whom he deliteth.
3.13: Blessed is the man that findeth wisedome, and the man that getteth understanding.
3.14: For the marchandise thereof is better then the marchandise of silver, and the gain thereof is better then gold.
3.15: It is more precious then pearles: and all things that thou canst desire, are not to be compared unto her.
3.16: Length of dayes is in her right hand, and in her left hand riches and glory.
3.17: Her wayes are wayes of pleasure, and all her pathes prosperitie.
3.18: She is a tree of life to them that lay hold on her, and blessed is he that retaineth her.
3.19: The Lord by wisdom hath layde the foundation of the earth, and hath stablished the heavens through understanding.
3.20: By his knowledge the depthes are broken up, and the cloudes droppe down the dew.
3.21: My sonne, let not these things depart from thine eyes, but observe wisdom, and counsel.
3.22: So they shalbe life to thy soul, and grace unto thy neck.
3.23: Then shalt thou walk safely by thy way: and thy foot shall not stumble.
3.24: If thou sleepest, thou shalt not bee afraid, and when thou sleepest, thy sleep shalbe sweet.
3.25: Thou shalt not fear for any sudden fear, neither for the destruction of the wicked, when it cometh.
3.26: For the Lord shall be for thine assurance, and shall preserve thy foot from taking.
3.27: Withhold not the good from the owners thereof, though there be power in thine hand to doe it.
3.28: Say not unto thy neighbour, Go and come again, and to morow wil I give thee, if thou now have it.
3.29: Intend none hurt against thy neighbour, seeing he doeth dwell without fear by thee.
3.30: Strive not with a man causeless, when he hath done thee no harm.
3.31: Bee not enuious for the wicked man, neither chuse any of his wayes.
3.32: For the froward is abomination unto the Lord: but his secret is with the righteous.
3.33: The curse of the Lord is in the house of the wicked: but he blesseth the habitation of the righteous.
3.34: With the scornefull he scorneth, but hee giveth grace unto the humble.
3.35: The wise shall inherit glorie: but fooles dishonour, though they be exalted.

4.1: Hear, O ye children, the instruction of a father, and give ear to learn understanding.
4.2: For I doe give you a good doctrine: therefore forsake yee not my law.
4.3: For I was my fathers sonne, tender and dear in the sight of my mother,
4.4: When he taught me, and sayde unto me, Let thine heart hold fast my woordes: keep my commandements, and thou shalt live.
4.5: Get wisedom: get vnderstading: forget not, neither decline from the woordes of my mouth.
4.6: Forsake her not, and she shall keep thee: love her and she shall preserve thee.
4.7: Wisedome is the beginning: get wisedome therefore: and above all thy possession get understanding.
4.8: Exalt her, and she shall exalt thee: she shall bring thee to honour, if thou embrace her.
4.9: She shall give a comely ornamet unto thine head, yea, she shall give thee a crown of glorie.
4.10: Hear, my sonne, and receive my wordes, and the yeeres of thy life shalbe many.
4.11: I have taught thee in ye way of wisedom, and led thee in the pathes of righteousness.
4.12: Whe thou goest, thy gate shall not be strait, and when thou runnest, thou shalt not fall.
4.13: Take hold of instruction, and leave not: keep her, for she is thy life.
4.14: Enter not into the way of the wicked, and walk not in the way of evil men.
4.15: Avoid it, and goe not by it: turn from it, and pass by.
4.16: For they can not sleep, except they have done evil, and their sleep departeth except they cause some to fall.
4.17: For they eat the bread of wickedness, and drink the wine of violence.
4.18: But the way of the righteous shineth as the light, that shineth more and more unto the perfite day.
4.19: The way of the wicked is as the darkenes: they know not wherein they shall fall.
4.20: My sonne, hearken unto my wordes, incline thine ear unto my sayings.
4.21: Let them not depart from thine eyes, but keep them in the middes of thine heart.
4.22: For they are life unto those that find them, and health unto all their flesh.
4.23: Keep thine heart with all diligence: for thereout cometh life.
4.24: Put away from thee a froward mouth, and put wicked lippes far from thee.
4.25: Let thine eyes behold the right, and let thine eyelids direct thy way before thee.
4.26: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy waies be ordred aright.
4.27: Turn not to the right hand, nor to the left, but remooue thy foot from evil.

5.1: My sonne, hearken unto my wisedome, and incline thine ear unto my knowledge.
5.2: That thou maiest regard counsel, and thy lippes observe knowledge.
5.3: For the lippes of a strange woman drop as an honie combe, and her mouth is more soft then oyle.
5.4: But the end of her is bitter as wormewood, and sharp as a two edged sword.
5.5: Her feet goe down to death, and her steps take hold on hell.
5.6: She weigheth not the way of life: her paths are moveable: thou canst not know them.
5.7: Hear yee me now therefore, O children, and depart not from the wordes of my mouth.
5.8: Keep thy way far from her, and come not neere the door of her house,
5.9: Least thou give thine honor unto others, and thy yeeres to the cruel:
5.10: Least the stranger should be silled with thy strength, and thy labours bee in the house of a stranger,
5.11: And thou mourn at thine end, (when thou hast consumed thy flesh and thy bodie)
5.12: And say, How have I hated instruction, and mine heart despised correction!
5.13: And have not obeied the voyce of them that taught mee, nor enclined mine ear to them that instructed me!
5.14: I was almost brought into all evil in ye mids of the Congregation and assemblie.
5.15: Drink the water of thy cistern, and of the rivers out of the middes of thine own well.
5.16: Let thy fountaines flow foorth, and the rivers of waters in the streetes.
5.17: But let them bee thine, even thine onely, and not the strangers with thee.
5.18: Let thy fountain be blessed, and reioyce with the wife of thy youth.
5.19: Let her be as the loving hind and pleasant roe: let her brests satisfie thee at all times, and delite in her love continually.
5.20: For why shouldest thou delite, my sonne, in a strange woman, or embrace the bosom of a stranger?
5.21: For the waies of man are before the eyes of the Lord, and he pondereth all his pathes.
5.22: His own iniquities shall take the wicked himself, and he shall be holden with the cordes of his own sinne.
5.23: Hee shall die for fault of instruction, and shall goe astray through his great follie.

6.1: My sonne, if thou be surety for thy neighbour, and hast striken hands with the stranger,
6.2: Thou art snared with the wordes of thy mouth: thou art even taken with the woordes of thine own mouth.
6.3: Doe this now, my sonne, and deliver thy self: seeing thou art come into the hand of thy neighbour, goe, and humble thy self, and sollicite thy friends.
6.4: Give no sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids.
6.5: Deliver thy self as a doe from the hand of the hunter, and as a bird from the hand of the fouler.
6.6: Goe to the pismire, O sluggard: behold her waies, and be wise.
6.7: For she having no guide, gouernour, nor ruler,
6.8: Prepareth her meat in the sommer, and gathereth her food in harvest.
6.9: How long wilt thou sleep, O sluggard? when wilt thou arise out of thy sleep?
6.10: Yet a litle sleep, a litle slumber, a litle folding of the hands to sleep.
6.11: Therefore thy pouertie cometh as one that travaileth by the way, and thy necessitie like an armed man.
6.12: The vnthriftie man and the wicked man walketh with a froward mouth.
6.13: He maketh a sign with his eyes: he signifieth with his feet: he instructeth with his fingers.
6.14: Lewd things are in his heart: he imagineth evil at all times, and raiseth up contentions.
6.15: Therefore shall his destruction come speedily: hee shall be destroyed suddenly without recouerie.
6.16: These six things doeth the Lord hate: yea, his soul abhorreth seven:
6.17: The hautie eyes, a lying tongue, and the hands that shed innocent blood,
6.18: An heart that imagineth wicked enterprises, feet that be swift in running to mischief,
6.19: A false witness that speaketh lyes, and him that rayseth up contentions among brethren.
6.20: My sonne, keep thy fathers commandement, and forsake not thy mothers instruction.
6.21: Bind them alway upon thine heart, and tye them about thy neck.
6.22: It shall lead thee, when thou walkest: it shall watch for thee, when thou sleepest, and when thou wakest, it shall talk with thee.
6.23: For the commandement is a lanterne, and instruction a light: and corrections for instruction are the way of life,
6.24: To keep thee from the wicked woman, and from ye flatterie of ye tongue of a strange woman.
6.25: Desire not her beautie in thine heart, neither let her take thee with her eye lids.
6.26: For because of the whorish woman a man is brought to a morsel of bread, and a woman wil hunt for the precious life of a man.
6.27: Can a man take fire in his bosom, and his clothes not be burnt?
6.28: Or can a man go upon coales, and his feet not be burnt?
6.29: So he that goeth in to his neighbours wife, shall not be innocent, whosoever toucheth her.
6.30: Men do not despise a thief, when he stealeth, to satisfie his soul, because he is hungrie.
6.31: But if he be found, he shall restore seven fold, or he shall give all the substance of his house.
6.32: But he that committeth adulterie with a woman, he is destitute of understanding: he that doeth it, destroyeth his own soul.
6.33: He shall find a wound and dishonour, and his reproch shall never be put away.
6.34: For ielousie is the rage of a man: therefore he will not spare in the day of vengeance.
6.35: He cannot bear the sight of any raunsome: neither will he consent, though thou augment the giftes.

7.1: My sonne, keep my wordes, and hide my commandements with thee.
7.2: Keep my commandements, and thou shalt live, and mine instruction as the apple of thine eyes.
7.3: Bind them upon thy fingers, and write them upon the table of thine heart.
7.4: Say unto wisedome, Thou art my sister: and call understanding thy kinswoman,
7.5: That they may keep thee from the strange woman, even from the stranger that is smooth in her wordes.
7.6: As I was in the window of mine house, I looked through my window,
7.7: And I saw among the fooles, and considered among the children a yong man destitute of understanding,
7.8: Who passed through the street by her corner, and went toward her house,
7.9: In the twilight in the evening, when the night began to be black and dark.
7.10: And behold, there met him a woman with an harlots behauiour, and subtil in heart.
7.11: (She is babling and loud: whose feet can not abide in her house.
7.12: Now she is without, now in the streetes, and lyeth in wait at every corner)
7.13: So she caught him and kissed him and with an impudent face said unto him,
7.14: I have peace offerings: this day have I payed my vowes.
7.15: Therefore came I forth to meet thee, that I might seek thy face: and I have found thee.
7.16: I have deckt my bed with ornaments, carpets and laces of Egypt.
7.17: I have perfumed my bedde with myrrh, aloes, and cynamom.
7.18: Come, let us take our fill of love until the morning: let us take our pleasure in daliance.
7.19: For mine husband is not at home: he is gone a journey far off.
7.20: He hath taken with him a bagge of silver, and will come home at the day appointed.
7.21: Thus with her great craft she caused him to yeelde, and with her flattering lips she entised him.
7.22: And he followed her straight wayes, as an oxe that goeth to the slaughter, and as a fool to the stockes for correction,
7.23: Till a dart strike through his liver, as a bird hasteth to the snare, not knowing that he is in danger.
7.24: Hear me now therefore, O children, and hearken to the wordes of my mouth.
7.25: Let not thine heart decline to her wayes: wander thou not in her paths.
7.26: For she hath caused many to fall down wounded, and the strong men are all slain by her.
7.27: Her house is the way unto ye grave, which goeth down to the chambers of death.

8.1: Doth not wisedome crie? and understanding utter her voyce?
8.2: She standeth in the top of the high places by the way in the place of the paths.
8.3: She cryeth besides the gates before the citie at the entrie of the doores,
8.4: O men, I call unto you, and utter my voyce to the children of men.
8.5: O ye foolish men, understand wisedome, and ye, O fooles, be wise in heart.
8.6: Give ear, for I will speak of excellent things, and the opening of my lippes, shall teach things that be right.
8.7: For my mouth shall speak the trueth, and my lippes abhorre wickedness.
8.8: All the wordes of my mouth are righteous: there is no lewdenes, nor frowardness in them.
8.9: They are all plain to him that will vnderstande, and streight to them that would find knowledge.
8.10: Receive mine instruction, and not silver, and knowledge rather then fine gold.
8.11: For wisdom is better then precious stones: and all pleasures are not to be compared unto her.
8.12: I wisdom dwell with prudence, and I find foorth knowledge and counsels.
8.13: The fear of the Lord is to hate evil as pride, and arrogancie, and the evil way: and a mouth that speaketh lewd things, I doe hate.
8.14: I have counsel and wisedome: I am understanding, and I have strength.
8.15: By me, Kings reign, and princes decree justice.
8.16: By me princes rule and the nobles, and all the judges of the earth.
8.17: I love them that love me: and they that seek me earely, shall find me.
8.18: Riches and honour are with me: even durable riches and righteousness.
8.19: My fruit is better then gold, even then fine gold, and my reuenues better then fine silver.
8.20: I cause to walk in the way of righteousnes, and in the middes of the paths of iudgement,
8.21: That I may cause them that love me, to inherit substance, and I will fill their treasures.
8.22: The Lord hath possessed me in the beginning of his way: I was before his workes of old.
8.23: I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning and before the earth.
8.24: When there were no depths, was I begotten, when there were no fountaines abounding with water.
8.25: Before the mountaines were setled: and before the hilles, was I begotten.
8.26: He had not yet made the earth, nor the open places, nor the height of the dust in the world.
8.27: When hee prepared the heavens, I was there, when he set the compass upon the deep.
8.28: When he established the cloudes above, when he confirmed the fountaines of the deep,
8.29: When he gave his decree to the Sea, that the waters should not pass his commandement: when he appointed the foundations of the earth,
8.30: Then was I with him as a nourisher, and I was dayly his delight reioycing alway before him,
8.31: And took my solace in the compass of his earth: and my delite is with the children of men.
8.32: Therefore now hearken, O children, unto me: for blessed are they that keep my wayes.
8.33: Hear instruction, and be ye wise, and refuse it not: blessed is the man that heareth mee, watching dayly at my gates, and giving attendance at the postes of my doores.
8.34: For he that findeth me, findeth life, and shall obteine fauour of the Lord.
8.35: But he that sinneth against me, hurteth his own soul: and all that hate me, love death.

9.1: Wisedome hath built her house, and hewen out her seven pillars.
9.2: She hath killed her vitailes, drawen her wine, and prepared her table.
9.3: She hath sent forth her maydens and cryeth upon the highest places of the citie, saying,
9.4: Who so is simple, let him come hither, and to him that is destitute of wisedome, she sayth,
9.5: Come, and eat of my meat, and drink of the wine that I have drawen.
9.6: Forsake your way, ye foolish, and ye shall live: and walk in the way of understanding.
9.7: He that reproveth a scorner, purchaseth to himself shame: and he that rebuketh the wicked, getteth himself a blot.
9.8: Rebuke not a scorner, least he hate thee: but rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee.
9.9: Give admonition to the wise, and he will be the wiser: teach a righteous man, and he will increase in learning.
9.10: The beginning of wisedome is the fear of the Lord, and the knowledge of holy things, is understanding.
9.11: For thy dayes shalbe multiplied by me, and the yeeres of thy life shalbe augmented.
9.12: If thou be wise, thou shalt be wise for thy self, and if thou be a scorner, thou alone shalt suffer.
9.13: A foolish woman is troublesome: she is ignorant, and knoweth nothing.
9.14: But she sitteth at the door of her house on a seat in the hie places of the citie,
9.15: To call them that pass by the way, that go right on their way, saying,
9.16: Who so is simple, let him come hither, and to him that is destitute of wisedome, she sayth also,
9.17: Stolen waters are sweet, and hid bread is pleasant.
9.18: But he knoweth not, that ye dead are there, and that her ghestes are in the depth of hell.

10.1: THE PARABLE OF SALOMON. A wise sonne maketh a glad father: but a foolish sonne is an heauines to his mother.
10.2: The treasures of wickedness profit nothing: but righteousness delivereth from death.
10.3: The Lord will not famish the soul of the righteous: but he casteth away the substance of the wicked.
10.4: A slouthfull hand maketh poor: but the hand of the diligent maketh rich.
10.5: He that gathereth in sommer, is the sonne of wisdom: but he that sleepeth in harvest, is the sonne of confusion.
10.6: Blessings are upon the head of the righteous: but iniquitie shall cover the mouth of the wicked.
10.7: The memorial of the just shalbe blessed: but the name of the wicked shall rotte.
10.8: The wise in heart will receive commandements: but the foolish in talk shalbe beaten.
10.9: He that walketh uprightly, walketh boldely: but he that perverteth his wayes, shalbe knowen.
10.10: He that winketh with the eye, worketh sorowe, and he yet is foolish in talk, shalbe beaten.
10.11: The mouth of a righteous man is a welspring of life: but iniquitie covereth the mouth of the wicked.
10.12: Hatred stirreth up contentions: but love covereth all trespasses.
10.13: In the lippes of him that hath understanding wisdom is found, and a rod shalbe for the back of him that is destitute of wisedome.
10.14: Wise men lay up knowledge: but ye mouth of the fool is a present destruction.
10.15: The rich mans goodes are his strong citie: but the fear of the needie is their pouertie.
10.16: The labour of the righteous tendeth to life: but the reuenues of the wicked to sinne.
10.17: He that regardeth instruction, is in the way of life: but he that refuseth correction, goeth out of the way.
10.18: He that dissembleth hatred with lying lips, and he that inuenteth slaunder, is a fool.
10.19: In many wordes there cannot want iniquitie: but he that refrayneth his lippes, is wise.
10.20: The tongue of the just man is as fined silver: but the heart of the wicked is litle worth.
10.21: The lippes of the righteous doe feed many: but fooles shall die for want of wisedome.
10.22: The blessing of the Lord, it maketh rich, and he doeth add no sorowes with it.
10.23: It is as a pastime to a fool to doe wickedly: but wisedome is understanding to a man.
10.24: That which the wicked feareth, shall come upon him: but God wil graunt the desire of the righteous.
10.25: As the whirlewinde passeth, so is the wicked no more: but the righteous is as an everlasting foundation.
10.26: As vineger is to the teeth, and as smoke to the eyes, so is the slouthful to them that send him.
10.27: The fear of the Lord increaseth the dayes: but the yeeres of the wicked shalbe diminished.
10.28: The patient abiding of the righteous shall be gladness: but the hope of the wicked shall perish.
10.29: The way of the Lord is strength to the upright man: but fear shall be for the workers of iniquitie.
10.30: The righteous shall never be remooued: but the wicked shall not dwell in the land.
10.31: The mouth of the just shall be fruitful in wisdom: but the tongue of the froward shall be cut out.
10.32: The lips of the righteous know what is acceptable: but the mouth of the wicked speaketh froward things.

11.1: False balances are an abomination unto the Lord: but a perfite weight pleaseth him.
11.2: When pride cometh, then cometh shame: but with the lowly is wisdom.
11.3: The vprightnes of the just shall guide them: but the frowardnes of the transgressers shall destroy them.
11.4: Riches auaile not in the day of wrath: but righteousnes delivereth from death.
11.5: The righteousnes of the upright shall direct his way: but the wicked shall fall in his own wickednes.
11.6: The righteousness of the just shall deliver them: but the transgressers shall be taken in their own wickednes.
11.7: When a wicked man dieth, his hope perisheth, and the hope of the vniust shall perish.
11.8: The righteous escapeth out of trouble, and the wicked shall come in his stead.
11.9: An hypocrite with his mouth hurteth his neighbour: but the righteous shall be delivered by knowledge.
11.10: In the prosperitie of the righteous the citie reioyceth, and when the wicked perish, there is ioye.
11.11: By the blessing of the righteous, the citie is exalted: but it is subuerted by the mouth of the wicked.
11.12: He that despiseth his neighbour, is destitute of wisedome: but a man of understanding will keep silence.
11.13: Hee that goeth about as a slanderer, discovereth a secret: but hee that is of a faithful heart concealeth a matter.
11.14: Where no counsel is, the people fall: but where many counsellers are, there is health.
11.15: Hee shall be sore vexed, that is suretie for a stranger, and he that hateth suretiship, is sure.
11.16: A gracious woman atteineth honour, and the strong men atteine riches.
11.17: Hee that is merciful, rewardeth his own soul: but he that troubleth his own flesh, is cruel.
11.18: The wicked worketh a deceitful work: but hee that soweth righteousnes, shall receive a sure reward.
11.19: As righteousnes leadeth to life: so hee that followeth evil, seeketh his own death.
11.20: They that are of a froward heart, are abomination to the Lord: but they that are upright in their way, are his delite.
11.21: Though hand ioyne in hand, the wicked shall not be unpunished: but the seed of the righteous shall escape.
11.22: As a iewell of gold in a swines snout: so is a fair woman, which lacketh discretion.
11.23: The desire of the righteous is onely good: but the hope of the wicked is indignation.
11.24: There is that scattereth, and is more increased: but hee that spareth more then is right, surely cometh to pouertie.
11.25: The liberal person shall have plentie: and he that watereth, shall also have rain.
11.26: He that withdraweth the corn, the people will curse him: but blessing shalbe upon the head of him that selleth corn.
11.27: He that seeketh good things, getteth fauour: but he that seeketh evil, it shall come to him.
11.28: He that trusteth in his riches, shall fall: but the righteous shall florish as a leaf.
11.29: He that troubleth his own house, shall inherit the wind, and the fool shalbe servant to the wise in heart.
11.30: The fruit of the righteous is as a tree of life, and he that winneth soules, is wise.
11.31: Behold, the righteous shalbe recompensed in the earth: how much more the wicked and the sinner?

12.1: He that loveth instruction, loveth knowledge: but he that hateth correction, is a fool.
12.2: A good man getteth fauour of the Lord: but the man of wicked imaginations will hee condemn.
12.3: A man cannot be established by wickedness: but the root of the righteous shall not be mooued.
12.4: A vertuous woman is the crown of her husband: but she that maketh him ashamed, is as corruption in his bones.
12.5: The thoughtes of the just are right: but the counsels of the wicked are deceitful.
12.6: The talking of the wicked is to lye in wait for blood: but the mouth of the righteous will deliver them.
12.7: God overthroweth the wicked, and they are not: but the house of the righteous shall stand.
12.8: A man shall be commended for his wisedome: but the froward of heart shalbe despised.
12.9: He that is despised, and is his own servant, is better then he that boasteth himself and lacketh bread.
12.10: A righteous man regardeth the life of his beast: but the mercies of the wicked are cruel.
12.11: He that tilleth his land, shalbe satisfied with bread: but he that followeth the idle, is destitute of understanding.
12.12: The wicked desireth the net of evils: but the root of the righteous giveth fruit.
12.13: The evil man is snared by the wickedness of his lips, but the just shall come out of aduersitie.
12.14: A man shalbe satiate with good things by the fruit of his mouth, and the recompence of a mans hands shall God give unto him.
12.15: The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that heareth counsel, is wise.
12.16: A fool in a day shall be knowen by his anger: but he that covereth shame, is wise.
12.17: He that speaketh trueth, will shew righteousnes: but a false witnes useth deceit.
12.18: There is that speaketh wordes like the prickings of a sword: but the tongue of wise men is health.
12.19: The lip of trueth shall be stable for ever: but a lying tongue varieth incontinently.
12.20: Deceit is in the heart of them that imagine evil: but to the counsellers of peace shall be ioye.
12.21: There shall none iniquitie come to the just: but the wicked are full of evil.
12.22: The lying lips are an abomination to the Lord: but they that deal truely are his delite.
12.23: A wise man concealeth knowledge: but the heart of the fooles publisheth foolishnes.
12.24: The hand of the diligent shall bear rule: but the idle shalbe under tribute.
12.25: Heauines in the heart of man doeth bring it down: but a good word reioyceth it.
12.26: The righteous is more excellent then his neighbour: but the way of the wicked will deceive them.
12.27: The deceitful man rosteth not, that hee took in hunting: but the riches of the diligent man are precious.
12.28: Life is in the way of righteousness, and in that path way there is no death.

13.1: A wise sonne will obey the instruction of his father: but a scorner will hear no rebuke.
13.2: A man shall eat good things by the fruit of his mouth: but the soul of the trespassers shall suffer violence.
13.3: Hee that keepeth his mouth, keepeth his life: but he that openeth his lips, destruction shall be to him.
13.4: The sluggard lusteth, but his soul hath nought: but the soul of the diligent shall have plentie.
13.5: A righteous man hateth lying wordes: but the wicked causeth slander and shame.
13.6: Righteousness preserveth the upright of life: but wickednes overthroweth the sinner.
13.7: There is that maketh himself rich, and hath nothing, and that maketh himself poor, having great riches.
13.8: A man will give his riches for the ransom of his life: but the poor cannot hear ye reproch.
13.9: The light of the righteous reioyceth: but the candle of the wicked shall be put out.
13.10: Onely by pride doeth man make contention: but with the well advised is wisdom.
13.11: The riches of vanitie shall diminish: but he that gathereth with the hand, shall increase them.
13.12: The hope that is deferred, is the fainting of the heart: but when the desire cometh, it is as a tree of life.
13.13: He that despiseth the word, hee shall be destroyed: but hee that feareth the commandement he shalbe rewarded.
13.14: The instruction of a wise man is as the welspring of life, to turn away from the snares of death.
13.15: Good understanding maketh acceptable: but the way of the disobedient is hated.
13.16: Every wise man will work by knowledge: but a fool will spread abroad folly.
13.17: A wicked messenger falleth into evil: but a faithful ambassadour is preseruation.
13.18: Pouertie and shame is to him that refuseth instruction: but hee that regardeth correction, shalbe honoured.
13.19: A desire accomplished deliteth ye soul: but it is an abomination to fooles to depart from evil.
13.20: He that walketh with the wise, shalbe wise: but a companion of fooles shalbe afflicted.
13.21: Affliction followeth sinners: but unto the righteous God will recompense good.
13.22: The good man shall give inheritance unto his childrens children: and the riches of the sinner is layde up for the just.
13.23: Much food is in the field of the poor: but the field is destroyed without discretion.
13.24: He that spareth his rod, hateth his sonne: but he that loveth him, chasteneth him betime.
13.25: The righteous eateth to the contentation of his mind: but the belly of the wicked shall want.

14.1: A wise woman buildeth her house: but the foolish destroyeth it with her own handes.
14.2: He that walketh in his righteousnes, feareth the Lord: but he that is lewd in his wayes, despiseth him.
14.3: In the mouth of the foolish is the rod of pride: but the lippes of the wise preserve them.
14.4: Where none oxen are, there the cribbe is emptie: but much increase cometh by the strength of the oxe.
14.5: A faithful witnes will not lye: but a false record will speak lyes.
14.6: A scorner seeketh wisdom, and findeth it not: but knowledge is easie to him that will vnderstande.
14.7: Depart from the foolish man, when thou perceivest not in him the lippes of knowledge.
14.8: The wisdom of ye prudent is to understand his way: but the foolishnes of the fooles is deceit.
14.9: The fool maketh a mock of sinne: but among the righteous there is fauour.
14.10: The heart knoweth the bitternes of his soul, and the stranger shall not medle with his joy.
14.11: The house of the wicked shalbe destroyed: but the tabernacle of the righteous shall florish.
14.12: There is a way that seemeth right to a man: but the issues thereof are the wayes of death.
14.13: Even in laughing the heart is sorowful, and the end of that mirth is heaviness.
14.14: The heart that declineth, shall be saciate with his own wayes: but a good man shall depart from him.
14.15: The foolish will beleeue every thing: but the prudent will consider his steppes.
14.16: A wise man feareth, and departeth from evil: but a fool rageth, and is careless.
14.17: He that is hastie to anger, committeth follie, and a busie body is hated.
14.18: The foolish do inherit follie: but the prudent are crowned with knowledge.
14.19: The evil shall bow before the good, and the wicked at the gates of the righteous.
14.20: The poor is hated even of his own neighbour: but the friendes of the rich are many.
14.21: The sinner despiseth his neighbour: but he that hath mercie on the poor, is blessed.
14.22: Doe not they ere that imagine evil? but to them that think on good things, shalbe mercie and trueth.
14.23: In all labour there is abundance: but the talk of the lippes bringeth onely want.
14.24: The crown of the wise is their riches, and the follie of fooles is foolishnes.
14.25: A faithful witnes delivereth soules: but a deceiver speaketh lyes.
14.26: In the fear of the Lord is an assured strength, and his children shall have hope.
14.27: The fear of the Lord is as a welspring of life, to auoyde the snares of death.
14.28: In the multitude of the people is the honour of a King, and for the want of people cometh the destruction of the Prince.
14.29: He that is slow to wrath, is of great wisdom: but he that is of an hastie mind, exalteth follie.
14.30: A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but enuie is the rotting of the bones.
14.31: He that oppresseth the poor, reprooueth him that made him: but hee honoureth him, that hath mercie on the poor.
14.32: The wicked shall be cast away for his malice: but the righteous hath hope in his death.
14.33: Wisedome resteth in the heart of him that hath understanding, and is knowen in the mids of fooles.
14.34: Justice exalteth a nation, but sinne is a shame to the people.
14.35: The pleasure of a King is in a wise servant: but his wrath shalbe toward him that is lewd.

15.1: A soft answer putteth away wrath: but grieuous wordes stirre up anger.
15.2: The tongue of the wise useth knowledge aright: but the mouth of fooles babbleth out foolishness.
15.3: The eyes of the Lord in every place behold the evil and the good.
15.4: A wholesome tongue is as a tree of life: but the frowardnes therof is the breaking of ye mind.
15.5: A fool despiseth his fathers instruction: but he that regardeth correction, is prudent.
15.6: The house of the righteous hath much treasure: but in the reuenues of the wicked is trouble.
15.7: The lippes of the wise doe spread abroad knowledge: but ye heart of the foolish doth not so.
15.8: The sacrifice of the wicked is abomination to the Lord: but the prayer of the righteous is acceptable unto him.
15.9: The way of the wicked is an abomination unto the Lord: but he loveth him that followeth righteousnes.
15.10: Instruction is evil to him that forsaketh the way, and he that hateth correction, shall die.
15.11: Hell and destruction are before the Lord: how much more the hearts of the sonnes of men?
15.12: A scorner loveth not him that rebuketh him, neither will he goe unto the wise.
15.13: A ioyfull heart maketh a chearefull countenance: but by the sorow of the heart the mind is heauie.
15.14: The heart of him that hath understanding, seeketh knowledge: but the mouth of the fool is fedde with foolishnes.
15.15: All the dayes of the afflicted are evil: but a good conscience is a continual feast.
15.16: Better is a litle with the fear of the Lord, then great treasure, and trouble therewith.
15.17: Better is a dinner of green herbes where love is, then a stalled oxe and hatred therewith.
15.18: An angrie man stirreth up strife: but hee that is slow to wrath, appeaseth strife.
15.19: The way of a slouthfull man is as an hedge of thornes: but the way of the righteous is plain.
15.20: A wise sonne reioyceth the father: but a foolish man despiseth his mother.
15.21: Foolishnes is joy to him that is destitute of understanding: but a man of understanding walketh uprightly.
15.22: Without cousel thoughts come to nought: but in the multitude of counsellers there is stedfastness.
15.23: A joy cometh to a man by the answer of his mouth: and how good is a word in due season?
15.24: The way of life is on high to the prudent, to auoyde from hell beneath.
15.25: The Lord will destroy the house of the proud men: but hee will stablish the borders of the widow.
15.26: The thoughts of ye wicked are abomination to the Lord: but the pure have pleasant wordes.
15.27: He that is greedie of gain, troubleth his own house: but he that hateth giftes, shall live.
15.28: The heart of the righteous studieth to answer: but the wicked mans mouth babbleth evil thinges.
15.29: The Lord is far off from the wicked: but he heareth the prayer of the righteous.
15.30: The light of the eyes reioyceth the heart, and a good name maketh the bones fat.
15.31: The ear that hearkeneth to the correction of life, shall lodge among the wise.
15.32: Hee that refuseth instruction, despiseth his own soul: but he that obeyeth correction, getteth understanding.
15.33: The fear of the Lord is the instruction of wisdom: and before honour, goeth humilitie.

16.1: The preparations of the heart are in man: but the answer of the tongue is of the Lord.
16.2: All the wayes of a man are clean in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the spirits.
16.3: Commit thy workes unto the Lord, and thy thoughts shalbe directed.
16.4: The Lord hath made all things for his own sake: yea, even the wicked for the day of evil.
16.5: All that are proud in heart, are an abomination to the Lord: though hand ioyne in hand, he shall not be unpunished.
16.6: By mercy and trueth iniquitie shalbe forgiven, and by the fear of the Lord they depart from evil.
16.7: When the wayes of a man please the Lord, he will make also his enemies at peace with him.
16.8: Better is a litle with righteousness, then great reuenues without equitie.
16.9: The heart of man purposeth his way: but the Lord doeth direct his steppes.
16.10: A divine sentence shalbe in the lips of the King: his mouth shall not transgress in iudgement.
16.11: A true weight and balance are of the Lord: all the weightes of the bagge are his work.
16.12: It is an abomination to Kings to commit wickednes: for the throne is stablished by justice.
16.13: Righteous lips are the delite of Kings, and the King loveth him that speaketh right things.
16.14: The wrath of a King is as messengers of death: but a wise man will pacifie it.
16.15: In the light of the Kings coutenance is life: and his fauour is as a cloud of the latter rain.
16.16: How much better is it to get wisedome then gold? and to get understanding, is more to be desired then silver.
16.17: The path of the righteous is to decline from evil, and hee keepeth his soul, that keepeth his way.
16.18: Pride goeth before destruction, and an high mind before the fall.
16.19: Better it is to be of humble mind with the lowly, then to deuide the spoyles with the proud.
16.20: He that is wise in his busines, shall find good: and he that trusteth in the Lord, he is blessed.
16.21: The wise in heart shall bee called prudent: and the sweetenesse of the lippes shall increase doctrine.
16.22: Vnderstading is welspring of life unto them that have it: and the instruction of fooles is folly.
16.23: The heart of the wise guideth his mouth wisely, and addeth doctrine to his lippes.
16.24: Fair wordes are as an hony combe, sweetenesse to the soul, and health to the bones.
16.25: There is a way that seemeth right unto man: but the issue thereof are the wayes of death.
16.26: The person that traueileth, traueileth for himself: for his mouth craveth it of him.
16.27: A wicked man diggeth up evil, and in his lippes is like burning fire.
16.28: A froward person soweth strife: and a tale teller maketh division among princes.
16.29: A wicked man deceiveth his neighbour, and leadeth him into the way that is not good.
16.30: He shutteth his eyes to devise wickednes: he moveth his lippes, and bringeth evil to pass.
16.31: Age is a crown of glory, when it is found in the way of righteousnes.
16.32: He that is slow unto anger, is better then the mightie man: and hee that ruleth his own mind, is better then he that winneth a citie.
16.33: The lot is cast into the lap: but the whole disposition thereof is of the Lord.

17.1: Better is a dry morsel, if peace be with it, then an house full of sacrifices with strife.
17.2: A discrete servant shall have rule over a lewd sonne, and hee shall deuide the heritage among the brethren.
17.3: As is the fining pot for silver, and the fornace for gold, so the Lord trieth the heartes.
17.4: The wicked giveth heed to false lippes, and a lyer hearkeneth to the naughtie tongue.
17.5: Hee that mocketh the poor, reprocheth him, that made him: and he that reioyceth at destruction, shall not be unpunished.
17.6: Childres children are the crown of the elders: and the glory of ye children are their fathers.
17.7: Hie talk becometh not a fool, much less a lying talk a prince.
17.8: A reward is as a stone pleasant in the eyes of them that have it: it prospereth, whithersoever it turneth.
17.9: Hee that covereth a transgression, seeketh love: but hee that repeateth a matter, separateth the prince.
17.10: A reproof entereth more into him that hath understanding, then an hundreth stripes into a fool.
17.11: A sedicious person seeketh onely evil, and a cruel messenger shall be sent against him.
17.12: It is better for a man to meet a bear robbed of her whelpes, then a fool in his follie.
17.13: He that rewardeth evil for good, evil shall not depart from his house.
17.14: The beginning of strife is as one that openeth the waters: therefore or the contention be medled with, leave off.
17.15: He that justifieth the wicked, and he that condemneth the just, even they both are abomination to the Lord.
17.16: Wherefore is there a price in the hand of the fool to get wisdom, and he hath none heart?
17.17: A friend loveth at all times: and a brother is borne for aduersitie.
17.18: A man destitute of understanding, toucheth the hand, and becometh suretie for his neighbour.
17.19: He loveth transgression, that loveth strife: and he that exalteth his gate, seeketh destruction.
17.20: The froward heart findeth no good: and he that hath a naughtie tongue, shall fall into evil.
17.21: He that begetteth a fool, getteth himself sorow, and the father of a fool can have no joy.
17.22: A ioyfull heart causeth good health: but a sorowfull mind dryeth the bones.
17.23: A wicked man taketh a gift out of the bosom to wrest the wayes of iudgement.
17.24: Wisdom is in the face of him that hath understanding: but the eyes of a fool are in the corners of the world.
17.25: A foolish sonne is a grief unto his father, and a heauines to her that bare him.
17.26: Surely it is not good to condemn the just, nor that ye princes should smite such for equitie.
17.27: Hee that hath knowledge, spareth his wordes, and a man of understanding is of an excellent spirit.
17.28: Even a fool (when he holdeth his peace) is counted wise, and hee that stoppeth his lips, prudent.

18.1: For the desire thereof hee will separate himself to seek it, and occupie himself in all wisdom.
18.2: A fool hath no delite in understanding: but that his heart may be discovered.
18.3: When the wicked cometh, then cometh contempt, and with the vile man reproch.
18.4: The words of a mans mouth are like deep waters, and the welspring of wisdom is like a flowing river.
18.5: It is not good to accept the person of the wicked, to cause ye righteous to fall in iudgement.
18.6: A fooles lips come with strife, and his mouth calleth for stripes.
18.7: A fooles mouth is his own destruction, and his lips are a snare for his soul.
18.8: The wordes of a tale bearer are as flatterings, and they goe down into the bowels of the belly.
18.9: He also that is slouthfull in his work, is even the brother of him that is a great waster.
18.10: The Name of the Lord is a strong tower: the righteous runneth unto it, and is exalted.
18.11: The rich mans riches are his strong citie: and as an hie wall in his imagination.
18.12: Before destruction the heart of a man is hautie, and before glory goeth lowlines.
18.13: He that answereth a matter before hee hear it, it is folly and shame unto him.
18.14: The spirit of a man will susteine his infirmitie: but a wounded spirit who can bear it?
18.15: A wise heart getteth knowledge, and the ear of the wise seeketh learning.
18.16: A mans gift enlargeth him, and leadeth him before great men.
18.17: He that is first in his own cause, is just: then cometh his neighbour, and maketh inquirie of him.
18.18: The lot causeth contentions to cease, and maketh a partition among the mightie.
18.19: A brother offended is harder to win then a strong citie, and their contentions are like the bar of a palace.
18.20: With the fruit of a mans mouth shall his belly be satisfied, and with the increase of his lips shall he be filled.
18.21: Death and life are in the power of ye tongue, and they that love it, shall eat the fruit thereof.
18.22: He that findeth a wife, findeth a good thing, and receiveth fauour of the Lord.
18.23: The poor speaketh with prayers: but the rich answereth roughly.
18.24: A man that hath friends, ought to shew him self friendly: for a friend is neerer then a brother.

19.1: Better is the poor that walketh in his vprightnes, then he that abuseth his lips, and is a fool.
19.2: For without knowledge the mind is not good, and he that hasteth with his feet, sinneth.
19.3: The foolishness of a man perverteth his way, and his heart freateth against the Lord.
19.4: Riches gather many friends: but the poor is separated from his neighbour.
19.5: A false witnes shall not be unpunished: and he that speaketh lyes, shall not escape.
19.6: Many reverence the face of the prince, and every man is friend to him that giveth giftes.
19.7: All the brethren of the poor doe hate him: how much more will his friends depart far from him? though hee be instant with wordes, yet they will not.
19.8: He that possesseth understanding, loveth his own soul, and keepeth wisdom to find goodness.
19.9: A false witnes shall not be unpunished: and he that speaketh lyes, shall perish.
19.10: Pleasure is not comely for a fool, much less for a servant to have rule over princes.
19.11: The discretion of man deferreth his anger: and his glory is to pass by an offence.
19.12: The Kings wrath is like the roaring of a lyon: but his fauour is like the dew upon ye grass.
19.13: A foolish sonne is the calamitie of his father, and the contentions of a wife are like a continual dropping.
19.14: House and riches are the inheritance of the fathers: but a prudent wife cometh of the Lord.
19.15: Slouthfulnes causeth to fall asleep, and a deceitful person shall be affamished.
19.16: He that keepeth the commandement, keepeth his own soul: but hee that despiseth his wayes, shall dye.
19.17: He that hath mercy upon the poor, lendeth unto the Lord: and the Lord will recompense him that which he hath given.
19.18: Chasten thy sonne while there is hope, and let not thy soul spare for his murmuring.
19.19: A man of much anger shall suffer punishment: and though thou deliver him, yet wil his anger come again.
19.20: Hear counsel and receive instruction, that thou mayest be wise in thy latter end.
19.21: Many deuises are in a mans heart: but the counsel of the Lord shall stand.
19.22: That that is to be desired of a man, is his goodnes, and a poor man is better then a lyer.
19.23: The fear of the Lord leadeth to life: and he that is filled therewith, shall continue, and shall not be visited with evil.
19.24: The slouthfull hideth his hand in his bosom, and wil not put it to his mouth again.
19.25: Smite a scorner, and the foolish wil beware: and reprove the prudent, and he wil understand knowledge.
19.26: He that destroyeth his father, or chaseth away his mother, is a lewd and shameful child.
19.27: My sonne, hear no more the instruction, that causeth to ere from ye words of knowledge.
19.28: A wicked witnes mocketh at iudgement, and the mouth of ye wicked swalloweth up iniquitie.
19.29: But iudgements are prepared for the scorners, and stripes for the back of the fooles.

20.1: Wine is a mocker and strong drink is raging: and whosoever is deceived thereby, is not wise.
20.2: The fear of the King is like the roaring of a lyon: hee that provoketh him unto anger, sinneth against his own soul.
20.3: It is a mans honour to cease from strife: but every fool will be medling.
20.4: The slouthfull will not plow, because of winter: therefore shall he beg in sommer, but have nothing.
20.5: The counsel in the heart of man is like deep waters: but a man that hath understanding, will draw it out.
20.6: Many men wil boast, every one of his own goodnes: but who can find a faithful man?
20.7: He that walketh in his integritie, is just: and blessed shall his children be after him.
20.8: A King that sitteth in the throne of iudgement, chaseth away all evil with his eyes.
20.9: Who can say, I have made mine heart clean, I am clean from my sinne?
20.10: Divers weightes, and divers measures, both these are even abomination unto the Lord.
20.11: A child also is knowen by his doings, whether his work be pure and right.
20.12: The Lord hath made both these, even the ear to hear, and the eye to see.
20.13: Love not sleep least thou come unto pouertie: open thine eyes, and thou shalt be satisfied with bread.
20.14: It is naught, it is naught, sayth the buyer: but when he is gone apart, he boasteth.
20.15: There is gold, and a multitude of precious stones: but the lips of knowledge are a precious jewel.
20.16: Take his garment, that is suretie for a stranger, and a pledge of him for the stranger.
20.17: The bread of deceit is sweet to a man: but afterward his mouth shalbe filled with gravel.
20.18: Establish the thoughtes by counsel: and by counsel make war.
20.19: He that goeth about as a slanderer, discovereth secrets: therefore meddle not with him that flattereth with his lips.
20.20: He that curseth his father or his mother, his light shalbe put out in obscure darkenes.
20.21: An heritage is hastely gotten at the beginning, but the end thereof shall not be blessed.
20.22: Say not thou, I wil recompense evil: but wait upon the Lord, and he shall save thee.
20.23: Divers weightes are an abomination unto the Lord, and deceitful balances are not good.
20.24: The steps of man are ruled by the Lord: how can a man then understand his own way?
20.25: It is a destruction for a man to deuoure that which is sanctified, and after the vowes to inquire.
20.26: A wise King scattereth the wicked, and causeth the wheel to turn over them.
20.27: The light of the Lord is the breath of man, and searcheth all the bowels of the belly.
20.28: Mercie and trueth preserve the King: for his throne shall be established with mercie.
20.29: The beautie of yong men is their strength, and the glory of the aged is the gray head.
20.30: The blewnes of the wound serveth to purge the evil, and the stripes within the bowels of the belly.

21.1: The Kings heart is in the hand of the Lord, as the rivers of waters: he turneth it whithersoever it pleaseth him.
21.2: Every way of a man is right in his own eyes: but the Lord pondereth the hearts.
21.3: To doe justice and iudgement is more acceptable to the Lord then sacrifice.
21.4: A hautie look, and a proud heart, which is the light of the wicked, is sinne.
21.5: The thoughtes of the diligent doe surely bring abundance: but whosoever is hastie, cometh surely to pouertie.
21.6: The gathering of treasures by a deceitful tongue is vanitie tossed to and from of them that seek death.
21.7: The robberie of the wicked shall destroy them: for they have refused to execute iudgement.
21.8: The way of some is perverted and strange: but of the pure man, his work is right.
21.9: It is better to dwell in a corner of the house top, then with a contentious woman in a wide house.
21.10: The soul of the wicked wisheth evil: and his neighbour hath no fauour in his eyes.
21.11: When the scorner is punished, the foolish is wise: and when one instructeth the wise, he wil receive knowledge.
21.12: The righteous teacheth the house of the wicked: but God overthroweth the wicked for their evil.
21.13: He that stoppeth his ear at the crying of the poor, he shall also cry and not be heard.
21.14: A gift in secret pacifieth anger, and a gift in the bosom great wrath.
21.15: It is ioye to the just to doe iudgement: but destruction shalbe to the workers of iniquitie.
21.16: A man that wandreth out of the way of wisdom, shall remain in the congregation of the dead.
21.17: Hee that loveth pastime, shalbe a poor man: and he that loveth wine and oyle, shall not be rich.
21.18: The wicked shalbe a ransom for the just, and the transgressour for the righteous.
21.19: It is better to dwell in the wilderness, then with a contentious and angry woman.
21.20: In the house of the wise is a pleasant treasure and oyle: but a foolish man deuoureth it.
21.21: He that followeth after righteousnes and mercy, shall find life, righteousnes, and glory.
21.22: A wise man goeth up into the citie of the mightie, and casteth down the strength of the confidence thereof.
21.23: He that keepeth his mouth and his tongue, keepeth his soul from afflictions.
21.24: Proud, hautie and scornefull is his name that worketh in his arrogancie wrath.
21.25: The desire of the slouthfull slayeth him: for his hands refuse to work.
21.26: He coveteth evermore greedily, but the righteous giveth and spareth not.
21.27: The sacrifice of the wicked is an abomination: how much more when he bringeth it with a wicked mind?
21.28: A false witnes shall perish: but hee that heareth, speaketh continually.
21.29: A wicked man hardeneth his face: but the just, he will direct his way.
21.30: There is no wisedome, neither understanding, nor counsel against the Lord.
21.31: The horse is prepared against the day of battell: but salvation is of the Lord.

22.1: A good name is to be chosen above great riches, and loving fauour is above silver and above gold.
22.2: The rich and poor meet together: the Lord is the maker of them all.
22.3: A prudent man seeth the plague, and hideth himself: but the foolish goe on still, and are punished.
22.4: The reward of humilitie, and the fear of God is riches, and glory, and life.
22.5: Thornes and snares are in the way of the froward: but he that regardeth his soul, will depart far from them.
22.6: Teach a child in the trade of his way, and when he is old, he shall not depart from it.
22.7: The rich ruleth the poor, and the borower is servant to the man that lendeth.
22.8: He that soweth iniquitie, shall reap affliction, and the rod of his anger shall fail.
22.9: He that hath a good eye, he shalbe blessed: for he giveth of his bread unto the poor.
22.10: Cast out the scorner, and strife shall go out: so contention and reproche shall cease.
22.11: Hee that loveth pureness of heart for the grace of his lippes, the King shalbe his friend.
22.12: The eyes of the Lord preserve knowledge: but hee overthroweth the wordes of the transgressour.
22.13: The slouthfull man saith, A lyon is without, I shall be slain in the street.
22.14: The mouth of strage women is as a deep pit: he with whom the Lord is angry, shall fall therein.
22.15: Foolishness is bound in the heart of a child: but the rod of correction shall drive it away from him.
22.16: Hee that oppresseth the poor to increase him self, and giveth unto the rich, shall surely come to pouertie.
22.17: Incline thine ear, and hear the wordes of the wise, and apply thine heart unto my knowledge.
22.18: For it shalbe pleasant, if thou keep them in thy bellie, and if they be directed together in thy lippes.
22.19: That thy confidence may be in the Lord, I have shewed thee this day: thou therefore take heed.
22.20: Have not I written unto thee three times in counsels and knowledge,
22.21: That I might shew thee the assurance of the wordes of trueth to answer the wordes of trueth to them that send to thee?
22.22: Rob not the poor, because hee is poor, neither oppress the afflicted in iudgement.
22.23: For the Lord will defend their cause, and spoyle the soul of those that spoyle them.
22.24: Make no friendship with an angrie man, neither goe with the furious man,
22.25: Least thou learn his wayes, and receive destruction to thy soul.
22.26: Be not thou of them that touch the hand, nor among them that are suretie for debts.
22.27: If thou hast nothing to pay, why causest thou that he should take thy bed from under thee?
22.28: Thou shalt not remooue the ancient bounds which thy fathers have made.
22.29: Thou seest that a diligent man in his business standeth before Kings, and standeth not before the base sort.

23.1: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before thee,
23.2: And put the knife to thy throte, if thou be a man given to the appetite.
23.3: Be not desirous of his deintie meates: for it is a deceiuable meat.
23.4: Travail not too much to be rich: but cease from thy wisdom.
23.5: Wilt thou cast thine eyes upon it, which is nothing? for riches taketh her to her wings, as an eagle, and flyeth into the heaven.
23.6: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire his deintie meates.
23.7: For as though he thought it in his heart, so will hee say unto thee, Eat and drink: but his heart is not with thee.
23.8: Thou shalt vomit thy morsels that thou hast eaten, and thou shalt lose thy sweet wordes.
23.9: Speak not in the eares of a fool: for hee will despise the wisdom of thy wordes.
23.10: Remooue not the ancient boundes, and enter not into the fieldes of the fatherless.
23.11: For he that redeemeth them, is mightie: he will defend their cause against thee.
23.12: Apply thine heart to instruction, and thine eares to the wordes of knowledge.
23.13: Withhold not correction from the child: if thou smite him with the rod, he shall not die.
23.14: Thou shalt smite him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.
23.15: My sonne, if thine heart be wise, mine heart shall reioyce, and I also.
23.16: And my reynes shall reioyce, when thy lips speak righteous things.
23.17: Let not thine heart bee enuious against sinners: but let it bee in the fear of the Lord continually.
23.18: For surely there is an end, and thy hope shall not be cut off.
23.19: O thou my sonne, hear, and bee wise, and guide thine heart in the way.
23.20: Keep not company with drunkards, nor with gluttons.
23.21: For the drunkard and the glutton shall bee poor, and the sleeper shalbe clothed with ragges.
23.22: Obey thy father that hath begotten thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.
23.23: Bye the trueth, but sell it not: likewise wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
23.24: The father of the righteous shall greatly reioyce, and hee that begetteth a wise child, shall have joy of him.
23.25: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall reioyce.
23.26: My sonne, give mee thine heart, and let thine eyes delite in my wayes.
23.27: For a whore is as a deep ditch, and a strange woman is as a narrow pitte.
23.28: Also she lyeth in wait as for a pray, and she increaseth the transgressers among men.
23.29: To whom is woe? to whom is sorowe? to whom is strife? to whom is murmuring? to whom are woundes without cause? and to whom is the redness of the eyes?
23.30: Even to them that tarie long at the wine, to them that goe, and seek mixt wine.
23.31: Look not thou upon the wine, when it is red, and when it sheweth his colour in the cup, or goeth down pleasantly.
23.32: In the end thereof it will bite like a serpent, and hurt like a cockatrise.
23.33: Thine eyes shall look upon strange women, and thine heart shall speak lewd things.
23.34: And thou shalt bee as one that sleepeth in the middes of the sea, and as hee that sleepeth in the toppe of the mast.
23.35: They have stricken mee, shalt thou say, but I was not sick: they have beaten mee, but I knew not, when I awoke: therefore will I seek it yet still.

24.1: Be not thou enuious against evil men, neither desire to be with them.
24.2: For their heart imagineth destruction, and their lippes speak mischief.
24.3: Through wisdom is an house builded, and with understanding it is established.
24.4: And by knowledge shall the chambers bee filled with all precious, and pleasant riches.
24.5: A wise man is strong: for a man of understanding encreaseth his strength.
24.6: For with counsel thou shalt enterprise thy war, and in the multitude of them that can give counsel, is health.
24.7: Wisdom is hie to a fool: therefore he can not open his mouth in the gate.
24.8: Hee that imagineth to doe evil, men shall call him an autour of wickednes.
24.9: The wicked thought of a fool is sinne, and the scorner is an abomination unto men.
24.10: If thou bee faint in the day of aduersitie, thy strength is small.
24.11: Deliver them that are drawen to death: wilt thou not preserve them that are led to be slain?
24.12: If thou say, Behold, we knew not of it: he that pondereth the heartes, doeth not hee understand it? and hee that keepeth thy soul, knoweth he it not? will not he also recompense every man according to his workes?
24.13: My sonne, eat hony, for it is good, and the hony combe, for it is sweet unto thy mouth.
24.14: So shall the knowledge of wisdom be unto thy soul, if thou find it, and there shall be an end, and thine hope shall not be cut off.
24.15: Lay no wait, O wicked man, against the house of the righteous, and spoyle not his resting place.
24.16: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth again: but the wicked fall into mischief.
24.17: Bee thou not glad when thine enemie falleth, and let not thine heart reioyce when hee stumbleth,
24.18: Least the Lord see it, and it displease him, and he turn his wrath from him.
24.19: Fret not thy self because of the malicious, neither be enuious at the wicked.
24.20: For there shall bee none end of plagues to the evil man: the light of the wicked shall bee put out.
24.21: My sonne fear the Lord, and the King, and meddle not with them that are sedicious.
24.22: For their destruction shall rise suddenly, and who knoweth the ruin of them both?
24.23: ALSO THESE THINGS PERTEINE TO THE WISE, It is not good to have respect of any person in iudgement.
24.24: He that saith to the wicked, Thou art righteous, him shall the people curse, and the multitude shall abhorre him.
24.25: But to them that rebuke him, shall be pleasure, and upon them shall come the blessing of goodness.
24.26: They shall kiss the lippes of him that answereth upright wordes.
24.27: Prepare thy work without, and make readie thy thinges in the field, and after, build thine house.
24.28: Be not a witnes against thy neighbour without cause: for wilt thou deceive with thy lippes?
24.29: Say not, I wil doe to him, as he hath done to mee, I will recompence every man according to his work.
24.30: I passed by the field of the slouthfull, and by the vineyard of the man destitute of understanding.
24.31: And lo, it was al growen over with thornes, and nettles had covered the face thereof, and the stone wall thereof was broken down.
24.32: Then I beheld, and I considered it well: I looked upon it, and received instruction.
24.33: Yet a litle sleep, a litle slumber, a litle folding of the handes to sleep.
24.34: So thy pouertie cometh as one that traueileth by the way, and thy necessitie like an armed man.

25.1: THESE ARE ALSO PARABLES of Salomon, which the men of Hezekiah King of Judah copied out.
25.2: The glorie of God is to conceal a thing secret: but the Kings honour is to search out a thing.
25.3: The heaues in height, and the earth in deepenes, and the Kings heart can no man search out.
25.4: Take the dross from the silver, and there shall proceed a vessell for the finer.
25.5: Take away the wicked from the King, and his throne shall be stablished in righteousnes.
25.6: Boast not thy self before the King, and stand not in the place of great men.
25.7: For it is better, that it be said unto thee, Come up hither, then thou to be put lower in the presece of the prince whom thine eyes have seen.
25.8: Goe not foorth hastily to strife, least thou know not what to doe in the end thereof, when thy neighbour hath put thee to shame.
25.9: Debate thy matter with thy neighbour, and discover not the secret to another,
25.10: Least he that heareth it put thee to shame, and thine infamie doe not cease.
25.11: A word spoken in his place, is like apples of gold with pictures of silver.
25.12: He that reprooueth the wise, and the obedient ear, is as a golden earering and an ornament of fine gold.
25.13: As the cold of the snow in the time of harvest, so is a faithful messenger to them that send him: for he refresheth the soul of his masters.
25.14: A man that boasteth of false liberalitie, is like cloudes and wind without rain.
25.15: A Prince is pacified by staying of anger, and a soft tongue breaketh the bones.
25.16: If thou have found hony, eat that is sufficient for thee, least thou be ouerfull, and vomit it.
25.17: Withdraw thy foot from thy neighbours house, least he be weary of thee, and hate thee.
25.18: A man that beareth false witnes against his neighbour, is like an hammer and a sword, and a sharp arrow.
25.19: Confidence in an vnfaythfull man in time of trouble, is like a broken tooth and a sliding foot.
25.20: Hee that taketh away the garment in the cold season, is like vineger powred upon nitre, or like him that singeth songs to an heavy heart.
25.21: If hee that hateth thee be hungry, give him bread to eat, and if he be thirstie, give him water to drink.
25.22: For thou shalt lay coles upon his head, and the Lord shall recompense thee.
25.23: As the Northwinde driveth away the rain, so doeth an angry countenance the slandering tongue.
25.24: It is better to dwell in a corner of the house top, then with a contentious woman in a wide house.
25.25: As are the cold waters to a weary soul, so is good newes from a far countery.
25.26: A righteous man falling down before the wicked, is like a troubled well, and a corrupt spring.
25.27: It is not good to eat much hony: so to search their own glory is not glory.
25.28: A man that refraineth not his appetite, is like a citie which is broken down and without walles.

26.1: As the snow in the sommer, and as the rain in the harvest are not meet, so is honour vnseemely for a fool.
26.2: As the sparowe by flying, and the swallow by flying escape, so the curse that is causeles, shall not come.
26.3: Unto the horse belongeth a whip, to the ass a bridle, and a rod to the fooles back.
26.4: Answer not a fool according to his foolishnes, least thou also be like him.
26.5: Answer a fool according to his foolishnes, least he be wise in his own conceit.
26.6: He that sendeth a message by the hand of a fool, is as he that cutteth off the feet, and drinketh iniquitie.
26.7: As they that lift up the legs of the lame, so is a parable in a fooles mouth.
26.8: As the closing up of a precious stone in an heap of stones, so is he that giveth glory to a fool.
26.9: As a thorn standing up in the hand of a drunkard, so is a parable in the mouth of fooles.
26.10: The excellent that formed all things, both rewardeth the fool and rewardeth the transgressers.
26.11: As a dog turneth again to his own vomit, so a fool turneth to his foolishnes.
26.12: Seest thou a man wise in his own conceit? more hope is of a fool then of him.
26.13: The slouthfull man sayth, A lyon is in the way: a lyon is in the streetes.
26.14: As the door turneth upon his hinges, so doeth the slouthfull man upon his bed.
26.15: The slouthfull hideth his hand in his bosom, and it grieveth him to put it again to his mouth.
26.16: The sluggard is wiser in his own conceit, then seven men that can render a reason.
26.17: He that passeth by and medleth with the strife that belongeth not unto him, is as one that taketh a dog by the eares.
26.18: As he that faineth himself mad, casteth fire brands, arrowes, and mortal things,
26.19: So dealeth the deceitful man with his friend and sayth, Am not I in sport?
26.20: Without wood the fire is quenched, and without a talebearer strife ceaseth.
26.21: As ye cole maketh burning coles, and wood a fire, so the contentious man is apt to kindle strife.
26.22: The wordes of a tale bearer are as flatterings, and they goe down into the bowels of the belly.
26.23: As silver dross ouerlayde upon a potsheard, so are burning lips, and an evil heart.
26.24: He that hateth, will counterfaite with his lips, but in his heart he layeth up deceit.
26.25: Though he speak fauourably, beleeue him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.
26.26: Hatred may be covered by deceit: but the malice thereof shall be discovered in the congregation.
26.27: He that diggeth a pit shall fall therein, and he that rolleth a stone, it shall return unto him.
26.28: A false tongue hateth the afflicted, and a flattering mouth causeth ruin.

27.1: Boast not thy self of to morowe: for thou knowest not what a day may bring forth.
27.2: Let another man prayse thee, and not thine own mouth: a stranger, and not thine own lips.
27.3: A stone is heauie, and the sand weightie: but a fooles wrath is heavier then them both.
27.4: Anger is cruel, and wrath is raging: but who can stand before enuie?
27.5: Open rebuke is better then secret love.
27.6: The wounds of a lover are faithful, and the kisses of an enemie are pleasant.
27.7: The person that is full, despiseth an hony combe: but unto the hungry soul every bitter thing is sweet.
27.8: As a bird that wandreth from her nest, so is a man that wandreth from his own place.
27.9: As oyntment and perfume reioyce the heart, so doeth the sweetenes of a mans friend by hearty counsel.
27.10: Thine own friend and thy fathers friend forsake thou not: neither enter into thy brothers house in the day of thy calamitie: for better is a neighbour that is neere, then a brother far off.
27.11: My sonne, be wise, and reioyce mine heart, that I may answer him that reprocheth me.
27.12: A prudent man seeth the plague, and hideth himself: but the foolish goe on still, and are punished.
27.13: Take his garment that is surety for a stranger, and a pledge of him for the stranger.
27.14: He that prayseth his friend with a loud voyce, rising earely in the morning, it shall be counted to him as a curse.
27.15: A continual dropping in the day of rain, and a contentious woman are alike.
27.16: He that hideth her, hideth the wind, and she is as ye oyle in his right hand, that uttereth it self.
27.17: Yron sharpeneth yron, so doeth man sharpen the face of his friend.
27.18: He that keepeth the fig tree, shall eat the fruit thereof: so he that waiteth upon his master, shall come to honour.
27.19: As in water face answereth to face, so the heart of man to man.
27.20: The grave and destruction can never be full, so the eyes of man can never be satisfied.
27.21: As is the fining pot for silver and the fornace for gold, so is every man according to his dignitie.
27.22: Though thou shouldest bray a fool in a morter among wheat brayed with a pestell, yet will not his foolishnes depart from him.
27.23: Be diligent to know ye state of thy flock, and take heed to the heardes.
27.24: For riches remain not alway, nor the crown from generation to generation.
27.25: The hey discovereth it self, and the grass appeareth, and the herbes of the mountaines are gathered.
27.26: The lambes are for thy clothing, and the goates are the price of the field.
27.27: And let the milk of the goates be sufficient for thy food, for the food of thy familie, and for the sustenance of thy maydes.

28.1: The wicked flee when none pursueth: but the righteous are bold as a lyon.
28.2: For the transgression of the land there are many princes thereof: but by a man of understanding and knowledge a realm likewise endureth long.
28.3: A poor man, if he oppress the poor, is like a raging rain, that leaveth no food.
28.4: They that forsake the Law, prayse the wicked: but they that keep the Law, set themselves against them.
28.5: Wicked men understand not iudgemnt: but they that seek the Lord understand all things.
28.6: Better is the poor that walketh in his vprightnesse, then hee that perverteth his wayes, though he be rich.
28.7: He that keepeth the Law, is a child of understanding: but hee that feedeth the gluttons, shameth his father.
28.8: He that increaseth his riches by vsurie and interest, gathereth them for him that will be merciful unto the poor.
28.9: He that turneth away his ear from hearing the Law, even his prayer shalbe abominable.
28.10: He that causeth the righteous to go astray by an evil way, shall fall into his own pit, and the upright shall inherit good things.
28.11: The rich man is wise in his own conceit: but the poor that hath understanding, can trie him.
28.12: When righteous men reioyce, there is great glory: but when the wicked come up, the man is tried.
28.13: He that hideth his sinnes, shall not prosper: but he that confesseth, and forsaketh them, shall have mercy.
28.14: Blessed is the man that feareth alway: but he that hardeneth his heart, shall fall into evil.
28.15: As a roaring lyon, and an hungry bear, so is a wicked ruler over the poor people.
28.16: A prince destitute of understanding, is also a great oppressour: but hee that hateth couetousnes, shall prolong his dayes.
28.17: A man that doeth violence against the blood of a person, shall flee unto the grave, and they shall not stay him.
28.18: He that walketh uprightly, shalbe saved: but he that is froward in his wayes, shall once fall.
28.19: He that tilleth his land, shall be satisfied with bread: but he that followeth the idle, shall be filled with pouertie.
28.20: A faythfull man shall abound in blessings, and he that maketh haste to be rich, shall not be innocent.
28.21: To have respect of persons is not good: for that man will transgress for a piece of bread.
28.22: A man with a wicked eye hasteth to riches, and knoweth not, that pouertie shall come upon him.
28.23: He that rebuketh a man, shall find more fauour at length, then he that flattereth with his tongue.
28.24: Hee that robbeth his father and mother, and sayth, It is no transgression, is the companion of a man that destroyeth.
28.25: He that is of a proud heart, stirreth up strife: but he that trusteth in the Lord, shall be fatte.
28.26: Hee that trusteth in his own heart, is a fool: but he that walketh in wisdom, shall be delivered.
28.27: He that giveth unto the poor, shall not lack: but he that hideth his eyes, shall have many curses.
28.28: When the wicked rise up, men hide them selves: but when they perish, ye righteous increase.

29.1: A man that hardeneth his neck when he is rebuked, shall suddenly be destroyed and can not be cured.
29.2: When the righteous are in authoritie, the people reioyce: but when the wicked beareth rule, the people sigh.
29.3: A man that loveth wisdom, reioyceth his father: but he that feedeth harlots, wasteth his substance.
29.4: A King by iudgement mainteineth ye countrey: but a man receiving giftes, destroyeth it.
29.5: A man that flattereth his neighbour, spreadeth a net for his steps.
29.6: In the transgression of an evil man is his snare: but the righteous doeth sing and reioyce.
29.7: The righteous knoweth the cause of the poor: but the wicked regardeth not knowledge.
29.8: Scornefull men bring a citie into a snare: but wise men turn away wrath.
29.9: If a wise man contend with a foolish man, whether he be angry or laugh, there is no rest.
29.10: Bloodie men hate him that is upright: but the just have care of his soul.
29.11: A fool powreth out all his mind: but a wise man keepeth it in till afterward.
29.12: Of a prince that hearkeneth to lyes, all his servants are wicked.
29.13: The poor and the usurer meet together, and the Lord lighteneth both their eyes.
29.14: A King that judgeth the poor in trueth, his throne shalbe established for ever.
29.15: The rod and correction give wisdom: but a child set a libertie, maketh his mother ashamed.
29.16: When the wicked are increased, transgression increaseth: but ye righteous shall see their fall.
29.17: Correct thy sonne and he will give thee rest, and will give pleasures to thy soul.
29.18: Where there is no vision, the people decay: but he that keepeth the Law, is blessed.
29.19: A servant will not be chastised with words: though he understand, yet he will not answer.
29.20: Seest thou a man hastie in his matters? there is more hope of a fool, then of him.
29.21: He that delicately bringeth up his servant from youth, at length he will be even as his son.
29.22: An angrie man stirreth up strife, and a furious man aboundeth in transgression.
29.23: The pride of a man shall bring him low: but the humble in spirit shall enioy glory.
29.24: He that is partner with a thief, hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and declareth it not.
29.25: The fear of man bringeth a snare: but he that trusteth in the Lord, shalbe exalted.
29.26: Many doe seek the face of the ruler: but every mans iudgement cometh from the Lord.
29.27: A wicked man is abomination to the just, and he that is upright in his way, is abomination to the wicked.

30.1: THE WORDS OF AGUR THE SONNE OF JAKEH. The prophecie which ye man spake unto Ithiel, even to Ithiel, and Ucal.
30.2: Surely I am more foolish then any man, and have not the understanding of a man in me.
30.3: For I have not learned wisedome, nor atteined to the knowledge of holy things.
